title: Growing without soil
subtitle: A classroom hydroponics project
intro: We’re building a classroom garden. First, we have to get the water moving.
question: What does a plant need when we take away the soil?
now: The frame and lights are up. We’re connecting four pairs of growing channels to one pump and reservoir.
next: Finish the tubing. Check for leaks. Test the flow through all four routes.
modelNote: Based on classroom photos. Dimensions and planting-hole spacing are approximate. Tubing shows the intended layout.

phases.title: What plants need
phases.description: Explore how food grows and the jobs our system must do.
phases.evidence: Notice-and-wonder observations and explanations of plant needs.

phases.title: Build the structure
phases.description: Design within our space and budget. Assemble the frame, channels, and lights.
phases.evidence: Build sketches, fitting counts, and reasons for design choices.

phases.title: Get water moving
phases.description: Connect the system. Test how height, slope, and fittings affect flow.
phases.evidence: Leak checks, observations, flow measurements, and revisions.

phases.title: Grow something
phases.description: Start lettuce. Observe how light, nutrients, and water conditions affect growth.
phases.evidence: Plant observations, growth records, and water measurements.

phases.title: Make it better
phases.description: Use the results to revise the system and explain our choices.
phases.evidence: A design defense, reflection, and a harvest celebration when the plants are ready.

lessons.title: How much land does food take?
lessons.description: Connect food choices to the space needed to grow food.

lessons.title: The six missing pieces
lessons.description: Identify plant needs and the jobs a hydroponic system has to do.

lessons.title: Vote and get ready
lessons.description: Name criteria, constraints, and the first steps of a build.

lessons.title: How many tees do we need?
lessons.description: Build branching models and use a pattern to explain fitting counts.
